message.content:
Below is a quick‑look at the **federal public holidays** that create “long weekends” in Canada for 2023.  
(Provincial/territorial holidays that fall on a weekday will also create a long weekend, but those vary by region – let me know if you’d like a province‑specific list.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long Weekend (Typical) |
|---------|-------------|-------------|------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday | Jan 1–2 (Sunday–Monday) |
| Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, SK, MB, QC) | Feb 20 | Monday | Feb 18–20 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Friday | Apr 7–9 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | May 20–22 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Saturday | Jul 1–3 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | Sep 2–4 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | Oct 7–9 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Thursday | Nov 10–12 (Thursday–Saturday) |

**Key points**

* **Federal holidays** are observed nationwide, so the above dates apply to all provinces and territories.  
* Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., Family Day in Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, BC, and Quebec; St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, etc.) that also create long weekends.  
* If you need a *province‑by‑province* breakdown, just let me know which provinces you’re interested in and I’ll compile the full list for you.
